# Player reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/player/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [PlayerController](#playercontroller)
- [WorldCursor](#worldcursor)

## PlayerController

`res://assets/scripts/player/PlayerController.gd`, extends [`ControllerBase`](../controllers/REFERENCE.md#controllerbase)

One player's controls: reads their devices, aims their camera, and gives their pawn input.

A first version: enough to drive a pawn and aim a camera. It survives with no pawn, as Unreal's does, and PossessionCoordinator creates it and tells it which pawn it has (pawn spec sections 5 and 6.2).

What it does:
- reads the player's devices, on this machine only
- holds the look direction, and tells the current camera arm where to look
- gives its pawn this tick's input as an InputCommand, when the pawn's ControllerManager asks (`take_input_command()`). Named actions (jump, sprint, ...) come from keys through `action_keys`.
- owns the player's one camera arm, which moves to each pawn they take (CameraMount, pawn spec 8.18)

What it doesn't do: move anything. The pawn's abilities do that, so an RTS or a flying pawn needs no special controller.

To drive it from a script, as a test or a replay viewer would, extend it and override the _read functions.

**Spectating.** PossessionCoordinator.spectate() lets go of the pawn and calls `start_spectating()`, and the player flies a FreeFlyCamera (`spectator_scene`) with the same keys and mouse, the view starting where the camera was. Taking a pawn stops it. Nothing starts it by itself: the game decides when a player spectates (between matches, waiting to respawn, after letting go of a pawn). The controls are in FreeFlyCamera's description.

What happens in odd cases (all checked in pawn/tests/possession_selftest.gd):
- No pawn: it keeps reading look input, and nothing moves.
- Spectating with a pawn still attached, as on a client between asking to let go and the server's answer: the keys fly the spectator and the pawn gets no movement or actions from them. The answer then lets go without stopping the spectating.
- An action missing from the project's input map: treated as not pressed.

### Settings and properties

- `look_mode: int` = `0`
- `mouse_sensitivity: float` = `0.0025`: Radians turned per pixel the mouse moves, in CAPTURED mode.
- `edge_zone: float` = `0.125`: How much of the screen counts as the edge, in SCREEN_EDGE mode, as a share of its width.
- `edge_turn_speed: float` = `150.0`: How fast the view turns at the very edge, in degrees per second, in SCREEN_EDGE mode.
- `click_to_move: bool` = `false`: On: clicking the ground walks there, along a nav path. The pawn's NavigationManager finds and follows it.
- `action_keys: Dictionary[StringName, StringName]` = `{...}`
- `spectator_scene: PackedScene`: The free-flying camera used while spectating (start_spectating()). Its root must be a FreeFlyCamera. Empty: a FreeFlyCamera with its default settings.
- `fly_up_key: StringName` = `&"move_jump"`: The keys (InputMap actions) that fly the spectator straight up and down: jump and crouch by default, so flying matches walking.
- `fly_down_key: StringName` = `&"move_crouch"`
- `camera: PlayerCamera` = `null`: The real camera. It holds where it is while there's no view to follow.
- `world_cursor: WorldCursor` = `null`: What the mouse or crosshair points at. It's off until something asks it.
- `look_yaw: float` = `0.0`: Where the player is looking, in radians.
- `look_pitch: float` = `0.0`

### Constants

- `LookMode.CAPTURED = 0`: The mouse is captured and turns the view, as in most action games.
- `LookMode.SCREEN_EDGE = 1`: The mouse stays free and the view turns when it nears the edge of the screen, as the old camera arm did.

### Functions

- `take_pawn(new_pawn: Pawn) -> void`: Takes this pawn, and lets go of any other. Null means none. Nothing else should call this: ask PossessionCoordinator.
- `start_spectating() -> void`: Flies a FreeFlyCamera with the player's keys and mouse, starting where the camera is now. Taking a pawn stops it. Games ask PossessionCoordinator.spectate(), which lets go of the pawn first and keeps track; calling this directly is for tests.
- `stop_spectating() -> void`: Stops flying. The camera holds where it is until there's a pawn. Games ask PossessionCoordinator.stop_spectating().
- `place_spectator(at: Transform3D) -> bool`: While spectating, moves the spectator to this place and faces it the same way, as for an overview point. False when not spectating, and nothing moves.
- `is_spectating() -> bool`: True while flying a FreeFlyCamera.
- `get_spectator() -> FreeFlyCamera`: The FreeFlyCamera, or null before the first time it spectates. For tests and debug tools.
- `take_input_command(_tick: int) -> InputCommand`: This tick's input, from the devices. It uses up the presses saved since the last tick, so call it once per tick.
- `move_to(world_point: Vector3) -> bool`: Walks the pawn to this place along a nav path, and in a straight line if there's no nav here. Keys take over from it. Passes on to the pawn's NavigationManager. False if there's no pawn, it has no NavigationManager, or there's no way there.
- `is_following_path() -> bool`: True while it's walking a path from move_to.
- `_read_move() -> Vector2`: Which way to go, with X to the right and Y backward, up to length 1.
- `_read_action_held(action: StringName) -> bool`: True while the key for this named action is down.
- `_read_action_pressed(action: StringName) -> bool`: True on the rendered frame the key for this named action went down.
- `_read_fly_up_down() -> float`: Spectating: up (1) or down (-1), from fly_up_key and fly_down_key (Space and Ctrl by default), so flying matches walking.
- `_read_look_extra() -> Vector2`: Any turning this frame beyond the mouse, as yaw and pitch in radians. For scripts, and later for gamepads.
- `_edge_turn(delta: float) -> float`: The old camera arm's way of turning: faster the closer the mouse is to the edge.

## WorldCursor

`res://assets/scripts/player/WorldCursor.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

What the mouse or crosshair points at in the world: a part of PlayerController.

It's Unreal's GetHitResultUnderCursor, with the polling made explicit. It does nothing and costs nothing until something asks.

Two ways to use it. One answer, right now, such as on a click:

```gdscript
var hit := controller.world_cursor.query_now()
```

Watching, such as a hover highlight or a placement preview, at a rate you choose:

```gdscript
controller.world_cursor.acquire(self, 20.0)   # 20 times a second. 0 means every frame
controller.world_cursor.hit_changed.connect(...)
controller.world_cursor.release(self)         # or just get freed or leave the scene, which counts as releasing
```

With several users, the fastest rate anyone asked for wins. When the last one is gone, it stops by itself.

An answer is a Dictionary: {"position", "normal", "collider"}. It's empty if the ray hit nothing, or if there's no camera. A captured mouse points at the middle of the screen, as a crosshair does. A free mouse points where it is.

Its ray is a physics query outside the physics step. That's safe with Godot's default setting, where physics doesn't run on its own thread. A project that turns that on would have to move this.

A note on rates: anything drawn at the cursor looks laggy at a low rate, so a visible cursor wants a high one.

### Settings and properties

- `collision_mask: int` = `3`: What the ray can hit. By default the ground's layer and the pawns' layer.
- `max_distance: float` = `1000.0`: How far the ray goes, in metres.
- `last_hit: Dictionary` = `{}`: The last answer. Empty means nothing is there, and it's only kept up to date while something is watching.

### Signals

- `hit_changed(hit: Dictionary)`: Sent when watching, each time there's a new answer.

### Functions

- `acquire(user: Object, times_per_second: float = 0.0) -> void`: Starts watching for this user, at this many times a second. 0 means every frame. Asking again changes its rate.
- `release(user: Object) -> void`: Stops watching for this user. When nobody is left, it stops altogether.
- `is_watching() -> bool`
- `get_user_count() -> int`
- `query_now() -> Dictionary`: One answer, right now, whoever else is watching.
- `_forget_freed_users() -> void`: Something that isn't a node can't say it's gone, so this notices.
